text:
Vantry Rail Systems said its maglev prototype hit 540 km/h during a pre-certification run on the Kestel test loop on 14 May, a company record and the fastest speed logged in its internal trial program.

The seven-car demonstrator completed three timed passes over 38.4 km, with average acceleration of 0.9 m/s² and peak energy draw of 19.6 MW. Vantry said the run was fully autonomous and within thermal limits.

Chief engineer Lio Arden said the result clears the company’s 2027 commercial target by “a wide margin.” For the rail sector, the milestone sharpens competition in ultra-high-speed ground transport, where suppliers are chasing lower ride times, lighter guideway systems and bankable power costs.
